title: brace-style: Having a catch method on a plain ES6 class throws `Closing curly brace does not appear on the same line as the subsequent brace style`

labels.name: accepted
labels.description: There is consensus among the team that this change meets the criteria for inclusion

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

**What did you do? Please include the actual source code causing the issue.**
We are mocking a promise interface within a backing object for our unit tests as part of a fake HTTP backend implementation.  It seems as though since v3.14.0 eslint thinks the catch method we have mocked here should always be a chained method call on a promise object.

<!-- Paste the source code below: -->
```js
export default class {

  constructor(data) {
    this.data = data;
  }

  then(callback) {
    this.data = callback(this.data);
    return this;
  }

  catch(callback) {
    callback({});
    return this;
  }
}
```

**What did you expect to happen?**
For eslint to recognise this as a plain ES6 class and lint it as such
